---
title: "Design and styles"
subtitle: "One palette for two shells"
toc: true
---

The atlas has two shells — the React explorer at `/map/frontend/` and this
Quarto site — and one design system. Colours live in CSS custom properties,
not in two copied stylesheets, so the dot on the Quarto map page is drawn with
exactly the same colour as the dot in the explorer.

## Where the styles live

| File | Contents | Loaded by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `tokens.css` | Light palette, spacing, radii, fonts | Explorer + site |
| `tokens-dark.css` | Dark palette (`prefers-color-scheme`) | Explorer only |
| `map.css` | Map, tooltip and shared panel/detail/badge components | Explorer + site |
| `app.css` | Explorer shell: header, sidebar, controls, modal | Explorer only |
| `analysis/styles.css` | Quarto typography, KPI cards, tables, map-page layout | Site only |

The site is light-only on purpose: the map and the report pages should look the
same when printed or pasted into a document, and the dark palette belongs to
the interactive explorer. Both shells read the same `--haz-*` ramp, so a
screenshot of either is directly comparable.

## Hazard ramp

Colour encodes the highest hazard level a facility reported, never the mass.

<div class="swatches">
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#aab4c0"></span><span class="swatch__name">0 · unassessed</span><code>--haz-0</code><span class="swatch__hex">#aab4c0</span></div>
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#d4dce5"></span><span class="swatch__name">1 · unclassified</span><code>--haz-1</code><span class="swatch__hex">#d4dce5</span></div>
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#e8b84a"></span><span class="swatch__name">2 · hazard-listed</span><code>--haz-2</code><span class="swatch__hex">#e8b84a</span></div>
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#e0783b"></span><span class="swatch__name">3 · high hazard</span><code>--haz-3</code><span class="swatch__hex">#e0783b</span></div>
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#bd3f5c"></span><span class="swatch__name">4 · very high</span><code>--haz-4</code><span class="swatch__hex">#bd3f5c</span></div>
  <div class="swatch"><span class="swatch__chip" style="background:#6f1d56"></span><span class="swatch__name">5 · known carcinogen</span><code>--haz-5</code><span class="swatch__hex">#6f1d56</span></div>
</div>

The ramp is sequential in lightness and hue (grey → yellow → orange → crimson
→ purple), so it stays readable for the most common forms of colour-vision
deficiency and survives greyscale printing as a lightness gradient. The levels
are ordered by the strength of the hazard evidence, not by mass.

## Type and spacing

- **Font:** `Segoe UI` → system UI → Helvetica/Arial, 15 px base, 1.55 line
  height on the site; the explorer uses 1.45 for denser panels.
- **Numbers:** tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) in tables,
  KPI cards and map tooltips, so digits line up between rows.
- **Scale:** 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 px (`--space-1` … `--space-6`), radii
  5 / 10 / 16 px (`--radius-1` … `--radius-3`), 15 px body, 1.55 rem KPI values.
- **Focus:** every interactive element keeps a visible `:focus-visible` outline
  in `--brand`; the map supports keyboard focus on circles.

The tokens are checked against this page by `analysis/check_tokens.py`, which
fails if a hex value shown above is missing from `tokens.css` or
`tokens-dark.css`.
